Better game than its predecessor but still full of the same issues it had. A 75/100 effort.

The good

Superbly rendered environments
Excellent voice acting
Same with the animations
A very decent story (if far-fetched)
Lots of hair-raising moments
Lots of good action sequences too, and a good selection of weapons to get the job done
Plenty of upgrade and crafting options
Lara is an appealing character. She's a human rather than a walking advertisement for silicone implants.

The bad

Close combat fighting is still problematical due to the whack camera angles
Enemy AI can range from passable to dumb to totally non-existent
Camera angles themselves can be a PITA. There's one instance where she's climbing a wall, and the camera goes AWOL way off the screen.
Too many Spielberg-ish cliffhanger moments
Main villain is an idiot
What Lara can climb or mantle is variable
Same with where she can go - lots of game walls and barriers
Backtracking involved if you want to explore places previously inaccessible due to a lack of the right weapon/tool

8/10

I bought this game imagining that I would get a nice 3D view of the play area. The tracking camera being replaced with the VR view while I guide Lara around the level in 3rd Person as normal.

No.

You have to play the actual game in normal 2D. The VR Supported bit is an annoying point and click adventure around the manor.

The result is that the VR experience feels tacked on and cheap and not part of the actual game.

Other than this it's a competent adventure-platformer.

I mark it as negative because I bought it on the promise of VR which it did not really deliver.

It is my mistake. I should have looked up a game review for the VR bit first. But I didn't and I don't want others to make the same mistake as I did.

Please note that my review is for very specific reasons. If you are not a VR gamer and love the Tomb Raider series then you should absolutely buy this game. I just can't give an "It Depends" rating.

I recently played Tomb Raider (2013), and I really enjoyed the experience. The story is one of the best parts of the game. It feels interesting and keeps you engaged throughout the journey, especially as Lara Croft develops as a character.

Considering that this game was released in 2013, I think the graphics still look pretty good. The environments, character animations, and action sequences are well designed, and the overall atmosphere makes the game enjoyable to play even today.

The gameplay is also fun, with a good mix of exploration, combat, puzzles, and adventure. Lara's journey feels challenging but rewarding, and the game does a great job of making you feel like you are surviving alongside her.

Overall, Tomb Raider (2013) is a really enjoyable action-adventure game with a great story, good gameplay, and impressive visuals for its time. I would definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys adventure and story-driven games.

Rise of the Tomb Raider raises the bar set by Lara’s last outing with a rollicking adventure story, strong villains, gorgeous vistas, and smart puzzles – go off the main path to find the best stuff in dastardly optional tombs. Though the mandatory combat doesn’t distinguish itself with challenging enemies unless you crank up the difficulty, Lara’s newfound versatility on the battlefield makes fighting a lot more fun. Once again it’s Lara herself, however, who steals the show, her complex ambitions and hardened resolve showing new sides to a character who has well and truly grown from survivor to the most fascinating action hero in video games today.

Compared to the first game, Rise of the Tomb Raider feels different right from the start. In Tomb Raider (2013), everything felt more raw and sometimes even creepy, like you were simply trying to survive. Here, Lara already feels like a more experienced adventurer (ehem… archaeologist/adventurer).

The gameplay is where you really notice the improvements. The graphics look better, the mechanics feel smoother, and everything is more polished. You can do more this time around, with more flexible combat, richer exploration, and improved movement. It basically takes everything from the first game and makes it even better.

The story also feels bigger, taking Lara deeper into mysteries and ancient secrets. You still get that same survival-adventure experience, but this time, Lara feels more confident and determined rather than someone who's just trying to make it out alive.

Overall, Rise of the Tomb Raider feels like the perfect evolution of the first game. It keeps everything that made the original enjoyable while improving almost every aspect of it. If you loved the first game, this is pretty much everything you'd want from a sequel.
